# Argus patches

Changed stationary ink outside all moving clips patches the existing composition backdrop after a bounded render, preserving chart surfaces and submitting both updates together. Paints overlapping chart ink and grouped foreground overlays keep the rebuild path. Frame-trace phase 15 records the patched area.

New paint revisions can reuse an existing chart tree when all stationary draws, image resources, clips and bar styles match. Frame-trace phase 14 records these replays. A one-shot `Scene::force_full_redraw` bypasses reuse and rebuilds the pixel caches for independent validation. The system-clipboard integration test is ignored by default and requires an explicitly isolated desktop.

Vertically rescaled charts use cropped opaque composition surfaces with the existing area-filter shader over a GPU-verified backdrop. Phase sheets exceeding the shared memory budget can use the same bounded path. Other eligible layers keep their cached position updates. Matching scratch textures and surfaces are reused across data revisions; incompatible spares are dropped before allocating replacements, and hide/resize/device loss release the pool. `gpu-chart-dynamic` reports the allocations, frame-trace phase 9 records updated pixels, and isolated `--test` processes can force this path with `ARGUS_GPUI_TEST_DYNAMIC_CHARTS=1`.

The static-prefix cache compares bounded snapshots of supported primitives across scene revisions. Identical prefixes remain valid; local changes repaint only the old and new ink bounds using a scissor and a rectangular clear, then copy the repaired pixels back to the cache. The prior dynamic region is restored when its geometry changes. Unsupported effects and large repairs use a complete paint. Snapshots are released with the prefix on hide, resize and device loss. `gpu-timing.repairedPixels` and `ARGUS_GPUI_DISABLE_PREFIX_REPAIR` support controlled comparisons. Retained chart trees validate image size and retry promotion after a vertical rescale settles.

Static foreground draws above retained charts are partitioned by primitive identity and checked against overlapping moving ink. Spatial draw-order levels can interleave disjoint content. A cropped, 16-texel-aligned BGRA scratch texture preserves the foreground, including translated glyph geometry. Opaque chart strips include overlapping foreground pixels; bar overlaps and costly strip plans use a foreground image in the same composition group. The foreground allocations share the existing budget and are released on hide, resize or device changes. Diagnostics report the plan, foreground bytes and group choice.

Large polychrome atlas pages fit the requested strip on 64-texel boundaries. A page enters the atlas after its first tile succeeds. Empty dedicated color pages are detached and can serve an exact-size replacement before presentation, with a limit of eight pages and 16 MiB. Presentation, hiding, resizing and device loss release unmatched pages. Diagnostics distinguish physical lifetimes (`gpu-atlas-page`) from replacement uploads (`gpu-atlas-reuse`).

The full-window MSAA and resolve textures for vector paths are allocated at the first path batch. A scene with no paths, a resize, or a hidden window releases these targets. Diagnostics report their creation and release through `gpu-path-targets`.

In a grid with many opaque chart clips, the column scan also compares each actual pixel with the reference column on the same row. Eligible charts use a single moving opaque base and a sparse DirectComposition surface for the differing columns. Only the correction lanes are initialized. They use the same subpixel phases and blended colors as ordinary backdrop strips. A failed virtual-surface update falls back to the ordinary opaque cache for the device. [DirectComposition virtual surfaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dcomp/nf-dcomp-idcompositiondevice-createvirtualsurface)

Thin rasters use eighth-pixel samples across uniform backdrop spans to preserve the antialiased ends of near-flat curves. Taller rasters retain their quarter-pixel spacing and texture budget.

Charts with an opaque backdrop cache reuse the same window-sized bitmap and composition root for full paints and cached layers. Pixel updates and layer changes commit together. A partial full-frame update copies the dirty rectangles from the current render target. Changing pages, hiding the window or losing the display/device releases the chart output when it is no longer applicable.

The opaque window mode presents ordinary frames through a BGRA HWND swap chain. A DirectComposition target covers that HWND only while a chart output is active. For marked fills in either window mode, a GPU pass checks the actual static prefix for opaque, horizontally identical columns across all visible ink rows. The renderer reads one flag per column without waiting on the GPU. Strips store the area-filtered chart blended over those pixels in alpha-ignored BGRA8 surfaces. Uniform spans share a scrolling transform. Dense glyph and grid edges share a fixed clip and store adjacent eighth-pixel scroll samples for each screen column. A second transform selects the same phase in every column. A strip can have foreground bars above it. Pending scans, intersections with earlier animated ink, complex or translucent backdrops, and out-of-cache movement use the normal scene. [D3D11 nonblocking readback](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d11/ne-d3d11-d3d11_map_flag)

Source: crates.io `gpui-pre-windows` 0.3.9, Zed revision `93d745668805029476e6d7fbb19652116fed51de`. The upstream Apache-2.0 license and package metadata are retained.

The package-local lockfile and unnormalized manifest are omitted; dependency resolution uses the workspace lockfile.

On standard SDR outputs, hardware adapters reporting HAGS support can promote a retained chart suffix into a DirectComposition tree. Hardware scheduling also requires the compositor-clock export, available on Windows 11. The tree owns an exact copy of the static prefix. The chart region uses a clamped identity color matrix to composite the prefix and moving charts into one image before blending with the window backdrop. Disjoint clips display the rest of the static prefix, including the window corners. It preserves batch order and clips area-filtered chart bitmaps and load bars independently. Between paints, chart movement updates visual offsets on the compositor. The quarter-pixel horizontal samples retain curve coverage in an FP16 scRGB bitmap. A bounded sheet uses the ordinary quad shader for bar heights with a maximum position error of 1/256 of a physical pixel. Complete paints, incompatible geometry, unsupported outputs and device errors use the swap chain. The active WDDM capability is queried for the rendering adapter, and a monitor change invalidates the output check. `gpu-chart-policy` diagnostics report this capability and the active scheduler. `ARGUS_GPUI_DISABLE_CHART_LAYERS=1` selects the swap chain for comparison. [DirectComposition visual effects](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dcomp/nf-dcomp-idcompositionvisual-seteffect)

Windows 11 resolves `DCompositionWaitForCompositorClock` from the already linked system library. A successful wait is a native frame tick even when it returns quickly. Occlusion or failures use the local refresh interval. Windows 10 retains the duration-guarded `DwmFlush` path. `gpu-frame-clock` reports the selected source, and `ARGUS_GPUI_USE_DWM_FLUSH=1` selects the legacy source for cadence comparisons.

The static background, FP16 chart bitmaps, bar sheets and a conservative FP16 allowance for the composition group's bounds share a budget of 1/64 of dedicated adapter memory, capped at 256 MiB. Adapters reporting no dedicated memory use a 48 MiB limit. A rejected tree reports its required bytes and budget in diagnostic mode. The polychrome sprite shaders preserve premultiplied color through filtering and source-over blending. Load-bar coverage ramps skip decorative gradient dithering so their solid interiors and antialiased edges do not depend on the coordinates of a cache allocation.

The atlas tracks the first and last inked rows of polychrome tiles when chart layers are enabled. The filter allocates just the contributing destination rows and a guard row at each edge, sampling at the original coordinates. Only changed offsets are submitted. Hiding a window detaches its chart tree, releases bar sheets and invalidates the saved background before the next visible draw.

After chart resources are released, the platform rechecks all tracked windows and calls [`IDXGIDevice3::Trim`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dxgi1_3/nf-dxgi1_3-idxgidevice3-trim) if the shared device is idle. A display-change notification defers the renderer's output check to its next draw, so COM message delivery during rendering can safely invalidate the cached SDR state.

Background composition subtracts earlier image masks from the restoration regions of later bars. Remaining copies are checked against every image after coalescing; incompatible ordering and overlap keep the copy-and-blend path. The `gpu-composition-reject` diagnostic reports these fallback cases. The window readback method uses the `test-support` feature gate, matching the GPUI platform trait and allowing geometry tests to run with the normal dependency features.

Rounded masks may extend past fractional image bounds. The composing shader covers the complete mask and restores cached background outside the image, so mask size no longer rejects this supported case. Geometry regressions cover fractional edges at multiple scales.

`ARGUS_GPUI_GPU_TIMING` enables sparse, delayed D3D11 timestamp/disjoint queries in `src/gpu_timing.rs`, the renderer and atlas. Reads retain the raw `S_FALSE` pending status, use `DONOTFLUSH`, validate frequency/disjoint state and recycle a bounded query pool. GPU phases, actual draw/copy/clear/resolve/upload counters and CPU Present1 duration are logged through a bounded asynchronous queue. Normal execution creates no timing queries. See the application's performance documentation for sample fields.

Steady two-texel footprints use four equally weighted linear samples at half-texel offsets. Scaled footprints and texture edges use the general paired-area weights. Both specializations execute behind explicit HLSL branches.

`src/directx_renderer.rs` batches per-draw constant parameters into reusable 64 KiB buffers. Devices supporting D3D11.1 constant-buffer offsets bind aligned ranges instead of repeatedly mapping a buffer for every draw. Unchanged batch layouts reuse the uploaded parameters. Device recreation clears these resources; drivers without offsetting retain the original binding path. Shaders, draw order, blending, antialiasing and sampling remain unchanged.

For bounds-only animations, the immutable prefix of the scene is copied as exact pixels from a cached texture. Batches at or after the first animated order still use the original rendering path. Complete paints, viewport changes and device recreation invalidate the cache; scenes with external surfaces use full rendering. Copying preserves output-merger state between batches. `ARGUS_GPUI_DISABLE_SCENE_CACHE` disables the pixel cache for controlled rendering comparisons.

Batches crossing the first animated draw order are split without reordering primitives. Retained frames restore the full animated masks, redraw the suffix and call `Present1` for that region; shrinking bars and translated images therefore erase their previous pixels. The dirty region is fully reconstructed on every frame, including intersections with earlier frames of the flip-sequential swap chain. Full draws and CPU readback still reconstruct the complete target; suffix shadows fall back to full presentation. See [DXGI incremental presentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddxgi/dxgi-1-2-presentation-improvements). Diagnostics include retained batches and dirty-region area.

The blend states for quads, shadows, underlines, sprites and path sprites accumulate coverage with "over" (`DestBlendAlpha = INV_SRC_ALPHA`) instead of adding the alphas. The premultiplied swap chain is composited by DWM over the window backdrop (Mica): with additive alpha a second translucent layer, or an antialiased edge on one, turned opaque and dropped the backdrop it should let through, so light-theme cards, controls, text and curves drawn on translucent surfaces came out grey and heavy. Opaque or single-layer content is unchanged.

Polychrome sprites marked `PolychromeSprite::AREA_FILTER` sample straight-alpha images by area in `src/shaders.hlsl`. `PREMULTIPLIED_AREA_FILTER` accepts premultiplied chart textures and pairs adjacent area weights into four hardware linear samples. Both paths cover one to three source texels per axis and treat pixels outside the atlas tile as transparent. `ARGUS_GPUI_DISABLE_LINEAR_AREA=1` selects the individual-texel reference sampler for the same premultiplied input; an explicit HLSL branch keeps the inactive texture path out of the draw. Bilinear sampling of such a raster point-sampled at some subpixel positions, which stair-stepped steep edges as the curve scrolled, and mixed straight colours with the transparent black around a stroke, which darkened its edges. Other sprites keep bilinear sampling. The background-composing variant of the sprite shader accumulates coverage with "over", matching the sprite blend state; it used to add the alphas, so retained frames covered more of the backdrop under light-theme translucent cards than full paints did. The source is rounded to 8 bits before composing, which keeps composed frames within two code values of fully painted ones (mostly one).

`src/alpha_correction.hlsl` applies the system's grayscale enhanced contrast to light text (brightness 50% and above) too. Upstream (adapted from Windows Terminal) fades it out for text brighter than 75%, while Argus keeps contrast enhancement for light text on dark backgrounds. Darker text replaces the DirectWrite contrast and gamma correction with Skia's mask gamma as Chromium applies it on Windows (gamma 1.2, contrast 0.2, text luminance quantised to 3 bits, background assumed to be its perceptual inverse). The release shader build also reruns when the included file changes.

`src/direct_write.rs` lays out a variable font requested between its named instances at exactly that weight on the `wght` axis, as browsers do; previously Segoe UI Variable at 330 drew its Semilight (350) instance and at 500 its Semibold (600) instance, and a fallback font followed the instance's weight (Chinese at 500 became Microsoft YaHei UI Bold instead of Regular). Weights that have a named instance, and fonts without a weight axis, keep DirectWrite's own matching: axis values reach the fallback fonts too, and non-variable fonts matched by axis can pick a lighter face with simulated bold. Glyph runs on faces the text system did not create (fallback fonts, variable instances) are rasterized with the face DirectWrite laid out, instead of a face matched again by family and weight, which lost axis values and simulations.

`src/events.rs` minimizes from the caption button by posting `WM_SYSCOMMAND` / `SC_MINIMIZE`, as the system caption does, instead of calling `ShowWindowAsync`; the window subclass that fades the window (`window_motion.rs` in the application) sees the request. Without a subclass, `DefWindowProc` minimizes the window exactly as before.

`src/events.rs` paints a new client size on `WM_NCCALCSIZE`, before the system applies it. The window takes its new rectangle when that message returns and DWM composes it at the next frame, while `WM_SIZE` arrives only at the end of `SetWindowPos` (4–13 ms later when another process resized the window). Upstream resized the swap chain on `WM_SIZE` and painted on the following `WM_PAINT`, so the new size showed the old content, with the window background in the uncovered strip and the caption buttons at their old place, for two or three refreshes. When a visible, non-minimized window with a frame callback changes its client size outside a draw, the handler resizes the renderer, reports the size to GPUI, draws and presents; the matching `WM_SIZE` then returns without repeating either. Minimizing, restoring and changes during a draw keep the `WM_SIZE` path. During that draw `GetClientRect` and `GetWindowPlacement` still describe the old rectangle. The handler now calls `DefWindowProc` itself for windows with a system title bar or in fullscreen, which it previously left to the caller with the same result. Frame-trace phase 16 records the painted size and phase 17 each `WM_SIZE` (1 when that size was already painted). `ARGUS_GPUI_DEFER_RESIZE_PAINT=1` restores the upstream order for comparison. DWM sometimes still shows a presented frame one composition after the new rectangle; waiting for the GPU before returning did not change this, and waiting for the compositor clock or presenting with sync interval 0 showed the new content one refresh before the new rectangle instead.

`src/window.rs` implements `PlatformWindow::set_content_zoom` (`Window::set_content_zoom` in gpui-pre). The window state keeps the DPI scale (`dpi_scale`) and the zoom apart; `scale_factor` is their product and converts everything in the client area: the content size, mouse, wheel, touchpad and drag-and-drop positions, the pointer position the native caption hit test uses, IME caret positions and the renderer's scene. Screen positions (`WM_MOVE`, the origin of `bounds` and `window_bounds`) and the minimum window size keep the DPI scale, so zoom changes neither where the window is nor how small it may get; the sizes in `bounds`, `window_bounds` and `resize` are content pixels, as the content size is. Setting the zoom recomputes the content size from the client rectangle (from the last size while minimized; `WM_SIZE` reports the real one on restore) and `WM_DPICHANGED` multiplies the new DPI scale by the zoom. Frame thickness and other system metrics remain in device pixels from `GetDpiForWindow`. At zoom 1 every conversion is unchanged.

`src/events.rs` handles `WM_IME_ENDCOMPOSITION`: if the input handler still has marked text and no `WM_IME_COMPOSITION` carrying `GCS_RESULTSTR` is queued for the window, the marked text is replaced with nothing, as a cancelled composition is. An input method can end a composition without a last `WM_IME_COMPOSITION`: through the IMM32 compatibility layer of Windows 11 (CUAS, with the Chinese layout active), `ImmNotifyIME(NI_COMPOSITIONSTR, CPS_CANCEL)` sends only `WM_IME_ENDCOMPOSITION`, which upstream does not handle, so the marked text stayed in the input as if the composition went on. A commit already queued behind the end replaces the marked text instead; the queue is peeked for posted messages only. Default processing follows in either case. Argus's process list relies on this to see a cancelled composition end (`src-gpui/src/frontend/type_search.rs`).

The alignment and capability checks follow [VSSetConstantBuffers1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d11_1/nf-d3d11_1-id3d11devicecontext1-vssetconstantbuffers1) and [D3D11_FEATURE_DATA_D3D11_OPTIONS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d11/ns-d3d11-d3d11_feature_data_d3d11_options). `ARGUS_GPUI_DIAGNOSTICS` reports the selected capability for owned tests. Remove the patch when equivalent behavior is available upstream.
